mechanisms.name: Sealed coverage denominator with finalize sweep
mechanisms.how: Each selected, non-deleted diff is registered as a CoverageItem, then SealSelected closes the set before resume reuse or dispatch. Each item moves once to completed, reused, failed or waived. A conflicting transition is an error, and repeating the same transition is a no-op. Finalize sweeps still-selected items into failed. The class comes from run_failure if set, else the pending cause (for example, budget), else unknown. Finalize then validates the partition and freezes the result as one object serialised to both the CLI JSON and session_end.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use the same pattern for AISEF's own review-coverage record: seal the policy-required set before calling OCR, then map OCR coverage into it. Required items that OCR never reports should be swept to INDETERMINATE, never silently passed.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not copy OCR's rule that a file with at least one comment in a stopped group counts as completed (agent.go:787-794), and do not let 'complete' imply a full review.

mechanisms.name: Pure, shared pre-dispatch selection with typed exclusion reasons
mechanisms.how: selectFiles(diffs) returns one decision per diff. Reasons are applied in this order: binary, secret, user exclude, user include override, extension allowlist, default path patterns, deleted, then the token-size ceiling. --preview and the run call the same function.
mechanisms.aisef_use: AISEF can run `ocr review --preview --format json` before the real run, diff its will_review set against AISEF's required set, and treat any required file that is excluded or missing as a coverage gap.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: OCR's defaults (tests, fixtures and .md excluded) are not AISEF's scope policy. Also, .gitignore and project rule.json are read from the working tree.

mechanisms.name: Content-independent item_id plus content-dependent fingerprint
mechanisms.how: item_id = sha256(join(['review', mode, normPath(old), normPath(new)], '\x00')). fingerprint = sha256(mode\0old\0new\0diffText.rstrip('\r\n')). source_artifact_sha256 = hashFields over (item_id, fingerprint) pairs sorted by item_id, where each field gets an 8-byte big-endian length prefix.
mechanisms.aisef_use: AISEF can recompute item_id from paths to join its required set with OCR coverage without trusting OCR's path strings, and can adopt length-prefixed field hashing for its own digests.

mechanisms.name: Resume admission before any session exists
mechanisms.how: ResolveIdentity repeats the diff load and selection with no side effects, and pins head, base and merge-base SHAs. ValidateResume compares mode, repository, source artifact and rule digest, and requires explicit flags for a provider or model change. Any mismatch rejects the whole resume, with no partial reuse.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use this as a model for AISEF's own child-run admission: check before creating anything, reject on mismatch, and record lineage. The parent/child lineage record (resume_identity.go:141-191) is also a useful shape.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Its identity leaves out runtime config, prompt template, tool version and effort. AISEF's identity should include them.

mechanisms.name: Terminal state derived only from coverage plus run_failure
mechanisms.how: computeTerminal ignores warnings and comment counts. A run-level failure (input, configuration, timeout, cancelled, budget, internal, unknown) forces failed. A 'pending failure cause' records a controlled truncation such as budget without failing the run.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Separate 'reviewer execution outcome' from 'delivery verdict'. Map OCR partial, failed or skipped to review INDETERMINATE or FAIL according to AISEF policy, never to PASS.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not copy the exit-code contract that exits 0 on partial.

mechanisms.name: Escalating tool-failure streak
mechanisms.how: A per-(task, tool) consecutive-failure counter returns a plain error on failure 1, an explicit 'second failure' message on failure 2, and from failure 3 on a fake success saying the call was skipped. It resets on success.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Treat any code_comment entry in tool_calls.failure_details as a possibly dropped finding. Surface it in the review record, or rerun.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not copy the 'pretend success' wording in any loop whose output feeds an acceptance decision.

mechanisms.name: Reason sanitisation floor
mechanisms.how: Before a failure or waive reason is stored in the manifest, it is coerced to valid UTF-8, stripped of control and C1 characters, redacted for URL userinfo, Bearer/Basic tokens and secret=value pairs, and capped at 500 runes.
mechanisms.aisef_use: AISEF can apply a similar redaction floor to any reviewer text it persists into evidence.

mechanisms.name: Retry report
mechanisms.how: An LLM retry report (ocr.llm-retry-report/v1) records each logical request with its attempts, error classes and outcomes. It is frozen at the run boundary and appears in JSON only when some request was retried or failed.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Keep it as optional provider-health diagnostics in AISEF's cost and incident record.

OCR ADAPTER CONTRACT (pinned to open-code-review v1.12.12 = 182898c; all references @182898c) 1. INVOCATION Preflight, no LLM call, no API key, no session (review_cmd.go:154-156, 504-528; preview.go:35-53): ocr review --repo --from --to --rule --preview --format json --output Review run (shared_flags.go:15-75, 201-220): ocr review --repo --from --to --rule --format json --audience agent --output --provider

--model --effort --max-tokens --max-tokens-budget --concurrency --timeout --no-filter --background "" Invocation rules: - Pass full 40-hex SHAs. A fresh run does not seal refs (agent.go:144-150, 585-600). - Range mode reviews merge-base(from,to)..to (diff/git.go:218-231). Commit mode reviews first-parent..commit (diff/git.go:233-242); commit mode also injects the commit message unless --background is non-empty (background_file.go:50-64). - Environment: HOME= holding only a controller-written .opencodereview/config.json (provider entry, no mcp_servers, no auth_token_cmd). Unset ANTHROPIC_* and OCR_LLM_* except the controller's own (llm/resolver.go:127-150; config_cmd.go:92-99, 335-378; review_cmd.go:530-600). - Delete or ignore /.opencodereview/ and .gitignore effects. The controller rule.json must contain a non-empty include or exclude so it outranks project and global filters (system_rules.go:351-369, 410-440; diff/git.go:435-454). - Use a new --output path each run. The file is created lazily and is not written if the run fails early (shared_flags.go:41-46). 2. EXIT AND STREAMS - Exit status is 0 or 1 only (main.go:21-32). 1 means Run returned an error or terminal_state=failed (review_cmd.go:326-352). Partial, skipped and complete all exit 0. - stdout or --output carries exactly one JSON object when the manifest exists or the run succeeded (review_cmd.go:292-306). - On a failed run with no manifest, stdout is empty and stderr carries a jsonOutput-shaped {status:"failed", summary, tool_calls, session_id} (output.go:669-695). - Progress lines never go to stdout in json mode (shared.go:379-386). - AISEF must never derive a verdict from the exit code. - Always pass --output <fresh file>, read only that file, and scrub OTEL_*, OCR_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and OCR_CONTENT_LOGGING.

4. VERSION PIN
- execution.ocr_version for official binaries is "v1.12.12" (release.yml:44-47; Makefile:13-20). It is not "1.12.12".
- The npm `ocr` launcher spawns a detached updater that runs `npm i -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review@<latest>` every 18 minutes unless OCR_NO_UPDATE is set (bin/ocr.js:89-110; scripts/update.js:142-160).
- Invoke the native opencodereview binary by absolute path with a pinned sha256, and also set OCR_NO_UPDATE=1.

- OTEL_*

mechanisms.name: Sectioned checkpoint template with per-section token budgets
mechanisms.how: There is one checkpoint.md per session with 11 fixed '## §N' sections, each with an italic instruction line, plus a project MEMORY.md with 4 sections. Budgets are kept as a header-to-token map, and token counts use chars/4. A background LLM 'checkpoint-writer' subagent rewrites the sections when token thresholds are crossed.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use as the shape of AISEF's advisory 'context pack' (intent, next action, files, errors, decisions, open notes), with fixed section keys and budgets. Keep it strictly non-authoritative.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not let the section prose carry identity or state (task status, branch, live resources). In AISEF those come from controller records. Do not copy the 'copy API tokens verbatim' instruction (checkpoint-writer.txt:54-57).

mechanisms.name: Budget enforcement at injection time
mechanisms.how: readBudgetedSectionAware / readBudgeted truncate the checkpoint (11k), memory (10k), notes (6k) and global memory (6k) when the rebuild context is built, and append a pointer hint to the full file.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Enforce context budgets deterministically at the point of injection. Do not rely on the summarizer obeying them. Record what was truncated in the journal.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: chars/4 estimation as the only budget measure when cost accounting matters. Use the provider's token counts for spend.

mechanisms.name: Post-write validation with bounded re-prompt (preStop hook)
mechanisms.how: After the writer stops, a plugin runs structural and budget validators. 'extract-required' makes the writer spill content into a spillover file; 'error' sends a reflection message. Re-entries are capped at 3, after which the writer settles as success.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Validate the summary against a schema and budget, with a small bounded retry. On final failure, mark the summary invalid, keep the previous valid one, and say so explicitly.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Accepting an invalid checkpoint as success after the cap. Validators that have drifted from the shipped template (no golden test linking them). An unused quarantine function.

mechanisms.name: Success-gated watermark
mechanisms.how: The parent session's last_checkpoint_message_id advances only when the writer actor's outcome is success. On failure the delta is covered again at the next threshold.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Same principle for AISEF journal pointers: an index or progress pointer moves only after its artifact is durably written and validated.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Gating only the pointer while the artifact is edited in place. AISEF should write to a temp file, validate, rename atomically, and record the digest in the journal before moving the pointer.

mechanisms.name: Rebuild context mixes DB-owned sections with the agent summary
mechanisms.how: On context rebuild, MiMo injects a SQL-sourced task ledger, the active-actor registry, verbatim recent user messages (FIFO-bounded and excluding prior rebuild boundaries), the agent-written checkpoint and memory, and a memory key index.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Good pattern: put a controller-rendered header (run_id, attempt_id, journal seq, candidate/contract digests, phase, open findings, budget spent) next to the agent narrative, and quote verbatim user and owner instructions from the record rather than from the summary.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Letting the summarizer mutate the 'DB-owned' ledger through the task tool (tool/task.ts:113,199-200; checkpoint.ts:400,987).

mechanisms.name: Role write sandbox inside a single write gate
mechanisms.how: Every file-mutating tool calls assertWriteAllowed. For agent 'checkpoint-writer', the resolved target must lie under the memory root, followed by a precise allowlist. dream and distill may write the memory root plus <worktree>/.mimocode. Other agents may not write the writer-reserved tasks/ paths.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Enforce role write boundaries in the tool or sandbox layer, keyed on a controller-assigned role, never on prompt text. AISEF's equivalent: the developer process cannot write the journal, the checkpoint, verifier inputs or the trusted runtime.

research.adapter_contract:
Design rules for AISEF controller-owned checkpoint and resume, derived from MiMo-Code @6babeb0 (minimal set).

CONTROLLER-OWNED (authoritative; written only by the controller, in storage the developer and summarizer processes cannot write):
1. Run record and journal: run_id, attempt_id, parent_run_id, journal seq, phase, plan/policy/contract digests, candidate digest (git tree id), budget spent (provider-reported tokens and money), decisions, open findings, operation IDs. MiMo lets the main agent write checkpoint.md (memory-path-guard.ts:127-139) and lets the writer mutate task status (tool/task.ts:199-200). AISEF must not allow either.
2. The journal is append-only, and every record carries seq, prev_hash, run_id, attempt_id and lease epoch. Recovery may drop only a torn LAST line, and must record that it did. Never truncate (contrast persistence.ts:292-297).
3. A change of script, plan, policy or contract starts a NEW child run with parent_run_id and the new digests. The parent journal and evidence stay frozen and readable. Nested sub-runs are pinned by content digest, not by name.
4. Exclusivity is a lease: an O_EXCL or flock lease file holding owner pid, host, start time and epoch, plus a heartbeat. Resume refuses while the lease is live; taking over a stale lease bumps the epoch, and records with an old epoch are rejected (fencing). A DB 'running' status is never proof of a dead owner (contrast runtime.ts:1539-1545).
5. Replay keys include everything that can change outcome or authority: prompt digest, role, resolved model id, tool or permission set, isolation mode, candidate digest, contract digest and harness version. Cached LLM outputs are hints. Probe results are never reused across different candidate or contract digests.
6. Decision inputs come only from controller-run, fixed probe commands with schema-checked output bound to the candidate digest. Agent-reported metrics (MiMo metricValue/guardPass) are advisory text.
7. Side effects (commit, merge, revert, publish, charge) are executed by the controller as two-phase operations: an intent record with op_id, the effect, then a result record. On resume, an op that has intent but no result is reconciled by OBSERVING state (git rev-parse, ref existence, remote state), never re-run blindly and never delegated to an agent (contrast research-experiment.js:131-133).
8. Resume preflight checks: lease, journal chain, artifact digests, git HEAD and tree against the last journaled candidate digest, environment identity, and pending ops. A mismatch means block, or a new lineage. Never continue silently.
9. Timeouts per agent call, per probe and per run are enforced by the controller. Option objects are schema-validated and unknown keys rejected (MiMo's timeout_ms vs timeoutMs bug silently removed the 30-minute bound).
10. No-progress ladder counters (attempts, consecutive no-gain, pivots) are controller state derived from journaled probe outcomes, with thresholds versioned in policy. Count only iterations that actually executed.

AGENT-SUMMARIZED (advisory context only; never grants permission and never decides PASS):
11. The context pack has fixed section keys (intent, next action, files, known errors, decisions, open notes) and per-section budgets enforced by deterministic truncation AT INJECTION, with truncation recorded. The controller prepends its own identity header (rule 1 fields), and the prose cannot override it.
12. The summarizer role writes only to the pack path bound to its own run_id and attempt_id. This is enforced in the write tool or sandbox on the realpath. The summarizer gets no shell, no task, state or journal tools, and no write access to the repo. The developer role cannot write the pack.
13. Pack commit: write to a temp file, then the controller validates (schema, budget, secret scan), then renames atomically and journals the digest. On failure the controller keeps the previous valid pack and marks the run 'context_degraded'. Do not accept the pack after N retries.
14. Secret policy: verbatim credentials are forbidden in packs and memory. Run a redaction scanner before persisting (MiMo's writer prompt asks for verbatim API tokens).
15. Validators carry a golden test against the shipped template, so the template and validator cannot drift apart (MiMo drift: checkpoint-validator.ts vs checkpoint-templates.ts).
16. Any LLM 'are we done' judge may only trigger another attempt. It fails closed (an error means not done), is capped, records the judge model, persists its state with the run, and never sets delivery_verdict.
17. If plan scripts exist, they run in a capability-only interpreter with deterministic seeds. That interpreter is NOT the isolation boundary for the agents it starts; agent isolation is a separate OS-level sandbox.
risks: Copying MiMo's journal semantics would bring in a destructive resume: on a script change it truncates the JSONL and reuses the runID (persistence.ts:292-297; runtime.ts:588,1562-1563), so the earlier evidence is lost.

Copying MiMo's resume lock would leave a cross-process double-run hole. The lock is a module-global in-process mutex, and a DB 'running' status counts as resumable, so two controllers could execute and append to the same run (runtime.ts:1528-1545; util/lock.ts).
Replay keys leave out tools, permissions and the resolved model (persistence.ts:22-40; runtime.ts:1116-1118). A cached result produced under different authority would be replayed as current.

Agent-reported metrics and an agent-executed, unverified revert in research-experiment (research-experiment.js:39-48,102-133). Copying the loop as-is would let the evaluated agent produce the numbers and the rollback.
The LLM goal judge uses the same model as the worker, fails open on error, and permits a stop after 12 re-entries (prompt.ts:4140-4149,4175-4188). It must never feed delivery_verdict.

Summarizer authority creep: the checkpoint writer gets the 'task' tool and can set any task done or abandoned in any session (checkpoint.ts:400,987; tool/task.ts:113,199-200). The main agent can write checkpoint.md and MEMORY.md (memory-path-guard.ts:127-139). An AISEF clone must keep both out of controller state.

Secret leakage into persistent memory: the writer prompt instructs verbatim copying of API tokens and env values into the cross-session MEMORY.md (checkpoint-writer.txt:54-57), and there is no redaction step.

Validator and template drift means checkpoint validation does nothing useful: it re-prompts on headers that do not exist and then accepts after 3 tries (checkpoint-validator.ts:27-36 vs checkpoint-templates.ts:1-57; actor/spawn.ts:455-466). 'We validate the checkpoint' is not evidence of quality.
The checkpoint file is not transactional: it is edited in place and only the watermark is gated (checkpoint.ts:1011-1033; spec :72,99). A crash mid-write can inject a partially edited summary.

The QuickJS sandbox and the lexical workspace jail constrain only the orchestrator script. Spawned agents have INHERIT tools on the host (runtime.ts:819-823), and symlinks escape the jail (workspace.ts:11-18). Citing MiMo's 'sandboxed runtime' (README.md:221) as isolation would be a false claim.
Silent option drops: the per-iteration timeout_ms is ignored (research-experiment.js:114 vs runtime.ts:649), so iterations can run up to the 12-hour script deadline and cost goes unbounded.

Maturity: the workflow tool is experimental and off by default (flag.ts:387-391), and its spec docs note failing runtime tests (context-budget-control.md:21). None of the workflow mechanisms has production evidence in the repo.
There is no measured evidence in the repo that checkpoints reduce tokens or improve task success. Any AISEF claim of savings from adopting these ideas would need its own measurement.
Licensing: MIT plus a separate USE_RESTRICTIONS.md (README.md:573) whose legal relationship to MIT is unclear. If code is vendored rather than re-implemented, the owner should review it.

verify.adapter_contract_corrections:
The rules are sound, and every MiMo citation in them checks out against the code @6babeb0. They need these corrections and additions.

(1) Rule 3: MiMo's script-sha check hashes the copy it persisted itself (runtime.ts:1551-1563). An edit to the source plan file is invisible to it. AISEF must digest the authoritative source (the plan or policy file in the repo or controller store) at launch, and compare against the source again at resume.

(2) Rule 5: add 'resolved model even when the call omits it' and 'workspace root'. MiMo hashes model:null when the ref is omitted (persistence.ts:35), and resume does not restore the run model or workspace (runtime.ts:539,1514). Run-level parameters must be persisted with the run and restored on resume, or the resume must refuse.

(3) Rule 9: also require that per-agent timeouts, lifecycle and agent caps, and money budgets are TREE-WIDE and inherited by nested sub-runs. MiMo children deliberately get fresh per-run caps and no timeout (runtime.ts:1300-1303), with maxDepth 8.

(4) Rule 11: per-section budgets must sum to at most the injection cap, and truncation must follow a declared priority, not file order. MiMo's sections total 15,100 against an 11,000 cap (checkpoint-templates.ts:88-100; checkpoint.ts:1340), and budgeted-read.ts:91-110 cuts the later sections first.

(5) Rule 12: also forbid agent writes to any cross-run or cross-project memory. MiMo's main agent can write global/MEMORY.md, which is injected into every project's rebuild (memory-path-guard.ts:5,197-207,222; checkpoint.ts:1355-1358,1484-1486) despite the comment 'Read-only from the agent side' (checkpoint-paths.ts:34-35). Memory-path writes must not bypass the permission layer (external-directory.ts:39,154-167).

(6) New rule: an authority grant made for a run is scoped to that run and its attempt and expires with it. Never persist it into a session-wide ruleset. MiMo's workflow manifest 'always' grant lands in the session ruleset and is inherited by every background agent in that session (runtime.ts:716-764). This is the INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY concern.

(7) New rule: plan or orchestration scripts and their workspace root are controller inputs, never model-authored tool arguments (contrast tool/workflow.ts:45-62,206,240).

(8) New rule: resume and cancel are authorized against the run owner. MiMo's tool and route resume any runID with no session or owner check (tool/workflow.ts:390-399; runtime.ts:1515-1582).

(9) New rule: tool whitelists fail CLOSED when role or actor metadata is missing (contrast prompt.ts:1763-1768). The default permission must be deny, not '*':'allow' (agent.ts:108-109).

(10) Rule 6/7 addition: every evidence row (metric, verdict, keep/revert) carries the candidate commit or tree digest observed by the controller. MiMo's results.tsv 'commit' column holds the strings kept/reverted, and 'reverted' is written whether or not the revert happened (research-experiment.js:61,136).

(11) Rule 13 addition: a persistence failure (journal append, script or sha stamp) must fail or degrade the run explicitly. MiMo Effect.ignore's recordStart, writeScript and appendJournalSync (runtime.ts:570-579,1141-1143).

(12) Rule 16: 'fails closed' must be tested for transport and parse errors as well as typed errors. MiMo's fail-open applies only to the typed-error channel, so its behaviour on provider rejection is unverified (goal.ts:235; prompt.ts:4143).
missed: CODE: the checkpoint per-section budgets total 15,100 tokens, but the whole-file validator budget and the injection cap are 11,000 (checkpoint-templates.ts:86-100 says '~11K' wrongly; checkpoint-retry.ts:75; checkpoint.ts:1340). Truncation at injection runs in file order (budgeted-read.ts:91-110), so §9-§11 are dropped first. README.md:159 'importance ranking' is not what this code path does.

CODE: the main agent can write global/MEMORY.md under the memory root. Scope 'global' is valid (memory-path-guard.ts:5,197-207) and only sessions/<sid>/tasks is reserved (:134-139). That file is injected into every project's rebuild context (checkpoint.ts:1355-1358,1484-1486), although checkpoint-paths.ts:34-35 calls it 'Read-only from the agent side'. Agent-written text therefore persists across projects, and memory-tree writes skip both the external_directory and edit permission prompts (external-directory.ts:39,154-167).

CODE: workflow manifest permissions are asked once at launch, and an 'always' grant lands in the SESSION ruleset, inherited by every background subagent in that session, not only the workflow's agents (runtime.ts:716-764). Authority widens beyond the run, which matters for INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY.

CODE: the default permission is '*':'allow' (agent.ts:108-109), and the 'general' agent used by workflows is defaults+user (agent.ts:227-233). Workflow agents with INHERIT tools therefore run bash and edit with no prompt unless the user configured otherwise.

CODE: the workflow tool accepts a model-authored inline script and a model-chosen workspace (jail root) (tool/workflow.ts:45-62,206,240). The orchestration program and its file jail are both agent-controlled inputs.

CODE: resume does not restore the run's model, workspace, concurrency or deadline (runtime.ts:539,1514). Combined with journal keys that hash model:null when it is omitted (persistence.ts:35), results replay across a different model or workspace.
CODE: nested child workflows deliberately get fresh per-run lifecycle caps and no per-agent timeout (runtime.ts:1300-1303), up to maxDepth 8 (:611). MiMo has no tree-wide agent, time or cost bound.

CODE: resume and cancel through the agent tool and the HTTP route take any runID with no session or owner check; the relaunch uses the row's sessionID (tool/workflow.ts:383-399; runtime.ts:1515-1582).
CODE: the per-actor tool whitelist fails OPEN when the actor row is missing (prompt.ts:1763-1768).
CODE: research-experiment's 3-pivot stop cannot be reached at the default maxIters=15: pivots happen at iterations 6 and 11, and a third would need iteration 16 (research-experiment.js:30,77-90).

CODE: research-experiment results.tsv has a 'commit' column but writes 'kept'/'reverted' into it, never a commit id. 'reverted' is written whether or not the agent's revert happened (research-experiment.js:61,131-138). The evidence is not bound to a candidate digest.

CODE: persistence failures are silently ignored: recordStart, writeScript, recordTerminal and the journal appends are all Effect.ignore'd (runtime.ts:570-579,1141-1143; persistence.ts comments), so a run can continue with no durable record.

CODE: the writer instructions contradict each other. composeWriterPrompt tells the writer to write TASK_MEM_DIR/<id>/progress.md (checkpoint.ts:382-385), checkpoint-writer.txt:99 says DO NOT WRITE those files, and checkpoint.ts:400 lists task ops (progress, approve, batch_create) that the task tool schema rejects (tool/task.ts:81-92). Together with the N-01 validator drift, this is evidence that MiMo's checkpoint contract is not test-locked to its prompt.

CODE: ordinary (non-workflow) sessions do have loop detectors: the doom_loop permission ask (processor.ts:33,550-575), the repeated-step nudge (prompt.ts:243,4757-4783) and a flag-gated try-best detector (processor.ts:298-330). They are heuristic nudges, not progress measurement, which corrects the P-01 note.

INFERENCE: the goal judge's fail-open covers only typed failures. The model call runs inside Effect.promise (goal.ts:218-235), and the repo itself notes that catch combinators do not catch defects in this Effect version (runtime.ts:1548-1550). Provider or transport errors may propagate instead, which cannot be verified without the library or a test.

mechanisms.name: Content-addressed source snapshot
mechanisms.how: Resolve the branch to a full commit SHA, then `git archive --format=tar <sha>` into a create_new 0600 temp file in a 0700 directory owned by the euid. Stream SHA-256 and byte count, rename to <sha256>.tar, and on a collision re-verify the existing file and replace it if it is corrupt. The digest, path and size go into the run's BackendDescriptor and the commit SHA into StoredRun.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Freeze the candidate source as a content-addressed tar under the AISEF evidence store before any probe runs. Record the commit SHA, the tree SHA (`git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`), the archive SHA-256 and the size. Reject a dirty tree in code rather than in prompt text.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not use the archive digest as the identity for comparing sources across commits (commit id and mtime are embedded). Do not trust a cache by file name alone, as the SSH path does.

mechanisms.name: Verify-on-reload
mechanisms.how: from_run rebuilds the snapshot from the recorded digest, path and size, falls back to <data_dir>/source-snapshots/<digest>.tar, recomputes SHA-256 and size, and refuses on a mismatch. The supervisor marks the run Failed with a reason.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Re-verify the source, evaluator and policy digests every time an artifact is consumed: at probe time, on resume and at verdict. Make the size check mandatory and also check commit and tree SHA against the archive.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: The optional size check (skipped when 0 or unrecorded). Verifying on only one backend path.

mechanisms.name: Run in an extracted run directory
mechanisms.how: The run script is `mkdir -p repo; tar -xf <archive> -C repo; cd repo; <cmd>` in <data_dir>/local-runs/<run_id> (0700). It runs detached in its own process group with pid, pid_script, exit_code and log files; liveness is checked with ps plus a script-path match to defeat PID reuse; cancel TERMs the group.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Harness-owned probes (tests, evaluators) run against a fresh extraction of the frozen snapshot, never the developer's worktree. Keep the run dir, pid file and exit-code file layout so a restarted supervisor can re-attach.

research.adapter_contract:
These are design rules for AISEF 2.1 paired experiments, derived from OpenResearch. AISEF should reimplement the ideas in Python; it should not depend on `orx`.

1. Freeze before spend. Write the manifest, compute manifest_sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, no whitespace) with the hash field itself excluded, and store it append-only. Results go in a separate record that references manifest_sha256. Do not put results inside the manifest; the proposal's §6.2 list mixes the two.
2. Source identity. Refuse a dirty tree in code. Record commit, tree and archive SHA-256 plus size. Compare arms by tree SHA. Re-verify the archive's digest and size, mandatory with no 0 or unrecorded escape, at every point of use.
3. Extract every probe into a fresh run directory from the frozen archive, never the developer worktree. Probe processes get an explicit environment allowlist (names recorded, values never), not the user's env.
4. A paired experiment means two sibling manifests under one parent that differ only in the declared variable_under_test. A validator diffs the two manifests and fails if any other frozen field differs.
5. Model identity is tri-state (verified, provider_reported, unverified) with a reason, following OpenResearch's exact/unresolved/manual.
6. Limits and the stop rule are enforced by the controller, not by the adapter. The controller owns cancellation and kills the whole process group.
7. Persist the run handle (an operation id) before counting a launch as started.

mechanisms.name: Check-before-request limit gate
mechanisms.how: Before each model query, stop if n_calls>=step_limit, cost>=cost_limit or elapsed>=wall_limit. Otherwise increment n_calls, query, and add the returned cost.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use as the baseline arm's semantics, and as the documented lower-tier fallback when no reservation is possible. Declare the overshoot bound as max single-request cost x concurrency.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not treat it as a hard cap. Reserve before forwarding instead (see adapter_contract).

mechanisms.name: Per-step persistence in finally
mechanisms.how: try/except/finally inside the run loop calls save(output_path) after every step, including on exceptions, which are then re-raised.
mechanisms.aisef_use: The run record and ledger are flushed after each request or step, so a crash loses at most the in-flight unit.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Non-atomic write_text, and the in-flight request is not recorded. Use an append-only JSONL with a started record before forwarding, plus tmp+rename for snapshots.

mechanisms.name: Cost carried on the parse-failure exception
mechanisms.how: Model attaches cost and raw response to FormatError; the agent adds the cost in its except branch.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Rule: every billed response is costed whatever the downstream parse or tool outcome.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Charging through exception side-channels is easy to miss (bug #914). Meter at the transport layer instead.

mechanisms.name: Cost-tracking strictness switch
mechanisms.how: default = raise on missing/<=0 cost; ignore_errors = record 0
mechanisms.aisef_use: Keep the idea of failing closed on an unknown price before spend begins (preflight), but represent unknown explicitly.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Neither mode is acceptable. 0 for unknown disables the budget; abort-after-billing loses the spend record.

mechanisms.name: Harness-side workspace capture regardless of exit
mechanisms.how: ProgramBench finally tars /workspace and copies it out before saving the trajectory.
mechanisms.aisef_use: The baseline arm freezes the candidate snapshot from outside the sandbox after the client stops, and computes the digest and diff itself.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Running tar inside the agent-controlled container, and trusting an agent-printed submission (local.py:45-56).

mechanisms.name: Exit-message taxonomy via exceptions
mechanisms.how: InterruptAgentFlow subclasses carry an exit message (Submitted, LimitsExceeded, TimeExceeded, FormatError); uncaught exceptions are recorded by class name.
mechanisms.aisef_use: A small closed stop_reason enum owned by the harness: self_reported_done, budget_usd, budget_tokens, budget_requests, wall_time, client_error, infra_error, harness_error.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Free-form exception class names as status, and '' on KeyboardInterrupt.

mechanisms.name: Failed instances retained in batch output
mechanisms.how: Exceptions produce a preds entry with an empty patch; resume skips ids already present.
mechanisms.aisef_use: The experiment manifest keeps every run, including preflight, infra and product failures, and never re-runs silently.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Losing the trajectory when environment startup fails (agent None).

research.adapter_contract:
Design rules for AISEF 2.1 derived from mini-swe-agent@04d809c. These are proposals, not upstream features.

(A) Minimal cost ledger (V2-11)
1. Truth source: one append-only ledger.jsonl per run, written by a harness-owned metering proxy between the client and the provider. The client and the model never write it. mini's own counters understate spend (P7, N2-N4), so they are only cross-checks.
2. One record per HTTP attempt, retries included. Write `started` before forwarding and `finished` after. A killed run therefore still shows its in-flight attempts.
   Fields: run_id, arm, seq, logical_call_id|null, t_start/t_end (UTC + monotonic), outcome {ok, http_error, timeout, cancelled, refused_by_budget}, http_status, model_requested, model_reported (labelled provider-reported/unverified), tokens {input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, output, reasoning, reasoning_in_output: true|false|null}, token_source {provider_usage, estimated, absent}, usd {value|null, status: known|estimated|unknown, source: provider_reported | rate_card:<id>@<effective_date> | none}.
3. Invariants:
   - Unknown is never 0. A missing usage on a failed attempt gives tokens null and usd unknown.
   - Reasoning is added only when reasoning_in_output is false.
   - Price source and effective date are stored on every costed row.
   - 9router/combo routes with no rate card stay usd unknown, with token totals reported.
4. The run summary is a projection rebuildable from the JSONL: requests_total, requests_failed, sums per token class, usd_known, usd_estimated, n_usd_unknown, budget limits, stop_reason, recorded_overshoot = spend − limit (may be > 0), and declared_overshoot_bound.
5. Enforcement and overshoot bound:
   - Known prices: before forwarding an attempt, refuse if spent_known + spent_estimated + reserve > limit, where reserve = est_input_tokens × in_price + max_output_tokens × out_price (cache-write price if caching). Overshoot is then bounded by input-estimation error plus any provider usage beyond max_tokens.
   - Fallback (mini-style check-before-request, P7): bound = max single-attempt cost × max concurrency.
   - Unknown prices: only token and request caps are enforceable; say so, and do not claim a USD cap.
6. Wall time: the harness clock starts before the client is spawned. On expiry, kill the process group (pattern of local.py:72-92), cancel upstream requests and record them as cancelled. The bound is kill latency, not one step (N6).

(B) Minimal direct-agent baseline harness (arm A)
1. Same as the AISEF arms:
   - client binary and version
   - model route and provider settings
   - sandbox image
   - baseline commit
   - public task text only (no bundle, contract or hidden stimuli)
   - metering proxy and budget caps
   - wall time
2. Non-interactive with no human limit changes (contrast interactive.py:80-94). One fresh agent or process per run (N7). Record whether the agent can see its remaining budget (N8).
3. The agent's 'done' is recorded only as self_reported_done (mini's Submitted is just a sentinel line, local.py:45-56). In a finally, after the client exits for any reason, the harness snapshots the workspace from outside the sandbox and computes the candidate digest and diff itself (programbench.py:107-115 pattern, minus the in-container tar).
4. stop_reason comes from a closed enum set by the harness (see the exit-taxonomy mechanism), not from the client.
5. Persist run.json (tmp+rename), ledger.jsonl and the raw client transcript. Keep all failed runs in the manifest (swebench.py:157-176 pattern).
6. Evaluate with the same harness-owned probes and held-out evaluator as the AISEF arms, and only after the candidate is frozen.
7. Optional arm A' (mini as a secondary control): run DefaultAgent, not the interactive agent, with its LiteLLM traffic pointed at the same metering proxy. Whether model_kwargs api_base routes through the proxy is INFERENCE and not verified here. Treat mini's instance_cost/api_calls as cross-checks only. Pin commit 04d809c and its MIT notice.
risks: mini's instance_cost/api_calls understate true spend. Retries and failed attempts are uncosted, global-limit raises drop a billed call, and ignore_errors records 0. Using them as AISEF ground truth would bias the cost comparison in mini's favour.

On a 9router/combo route with no litellm price entry, mini either aborts after the first billed call (default) or records $0 with cost_limit disabled (ignore_errors). Both break a budget-matched comparison unless AISEF's proxy enforces the budget.
mini is not the 'same client' as AISEF's developer client. Results from arm A' cannot replace arm A.
The wall-time limit is soft. A single model call with up to 10 retries, or a long action, can overrun it, so harness-side kill is required for fair time budgets.
The default `mini` CLI is interactive and lets a human raise limits mid-run. Using it accidentally invalidates fixed budgets.

Upstream docs disagree with the code: final role 'user' vs 'exit', the meaning of api_calls, and $0 registry still raising. The proposal's link to the unpinned 'latest' docs site may drift further. Cite repo files at 04d809c.
The trajectory write is non-atomic and the in-flight request is never recorded. A copied pattern would lose crash evidence.
The submission is agent-printed text after a sentinel, and ProgramBench's tar runs inside the agent-writable container. Neither is a trusted candidate capture.

verify.adapter_contract_corrections:
Everything below was checked against 04d809c (HEAD = proposal commit). The contract is a set of design proposals, so only its factual anchors and assumptions can be verified.
1. (A5 fallback) 'bound = max single-attempt cost x max concurrency' holds only if AISEF's proxy gates every HTTP attempt. mini itself gates once per logical query (default.py:132-150), and up to 10 attempts run inside it (retry.py:21). A real mini-style bound is max_attempts x max attempt cost x concurrency. MSWEA_GLOBAL_* limits are checked after billing (models/__init__.py:25-31).
2. (A5 reservation) The reserve formula needs a max_output_tokens. mini's pinned configs set none: swebench.yaml:181-183 has only drop_params and parallel_tool_calls, and litellm_model.py:66-71 passes no max_tokens or timeout. The proxy must inject a cap (this changes the request, so record it as an arm difference) or use a declared provider maximum. Otherwise USD reservation is not well-defined (INFERENCE).
3. (A6) The killpg pattern at local.py:72-92 is per-command and host-only. DockerEnvironment's timeout (docker.py:116-124) kills only the `docker exec` client and leaves the in-container process running (INFERENCE from Docker semantics). Container teardown happens only in __del__ (docker.py:153-161), so it is non-deterministic. The harness must stop or kill the container itself, then cancel upstream requests. Pinned swebench.yaml sets no wall_time_limit_seconds while container_timeout defaults to 2h (docker.py:34), the exact failure #803/055c07a describes ('agent keeps issuing commands and burning API calls').
4. (B3) When copying the ProgramBench capture pattern, also check the capture's exit status, use a harness-owned path, and avoid the agent's login shell. programbench.py:54 ignores tar's returncode and docker-cps a fixed /tmp path, and the interpreter defaults to `bash -lc` (docker.py:38).
5. (B7) Routing can be stated partly as CODE, not only INFERENCE. model_kwargs are merged into litellm.completion(...) (litellm_model.py:66-71), and api_base in model_kwargs is the documented way to point at another endpoint (README docs/models/local_models.md:48-56,164-169). Only Litellm* and Portkey classes can be redirected. OpenRouterModel and RequestyModel hardcode their URLs (openrouter_model.py:60, requesty_model.py:64). Whether litellm uses api_base for every provider prefix and every retry remains INFERENCE. On a 9router/combo name litellm cannot price the call, so arm A' must run with cost_tracking=ignore_errors. That disables mini's cost_limit (cost 0, N2), and only the proxy enforces budget.
6. (B1/B2/B7, isolation) Importing minisweagent creates the user config dir and loads its .env into os.environ (__init__.py:26-36). Those values (MSWEA_COST_TRACKING, MSWEA_GLOBAL_*, MSWEA_MODEL_RETRY_STOP_AFTER_ATTEMPT, LITELLM_MODEL_REGISTRY_PATH, API keys) can silently differ per machine. Pin MSWEA_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR to a fresh dir and record the effective env. LocalEnvironment passes the full host environment, including provider keys, to every agent command (local.py:29) and into template vars (local.py:59). An agent could then call the provider directly and bypass the metering proxy (INFERENCE). Use DockerEnvironment, which forwards only forward_env/env (docker.py:107-112), and restrict network to the proxy. swebench.yaml leaves the default run_args ['--rm'] (docker.py:30, network on), whereas programbench.yaml:189-192 uses --network none.

DefaultAgent drops observations of actions already executed in a step when Submitted or another exception fires mid-step (default.py:154-157, unlike interactive.py:124-139), and parallel_tool_calls is on in swebench.yaml:183. The ProgramBench agent strips raw_output (programbench.py:33-43). Billed responses on RuntimeError paths are not persisted at all. mechanisms.name: Egress sidecar sharing the sandbox netns (dns proxy + nft default-deny)
mechanisms.how: Per sandbox, a sidecar container (cap_add NET_ADMIN, bridge network) starts first. The main container joins it with network_mode=container:<sidecar> and drops NET_ADMIN. The sidecar redirects port-53 traffic to a local DNS proxy that evaluates the policy. In dns+nft mode it also installs an inet output chain with policy drop, accepts established/lo/marked traffic and allow sets, and adds DNS-resolved IPs to a timed dynamic allow set. The policy can be changed at runtime via the token-protected :18080 /policy endpoint, proxied by the server's /sandboxes/{id}/networkpolicy.
mechanisms.aisef_use: This is the best reusable piece for V2-05. Give the developer sandbox a domain allowlist (model provider plus package mirrors only) and default-deny everything else, including the Docker bridge, the host gateway and other sandboxes. It can be used standalone with a plain hardened `docker run`: start the egress image as the sidecar, run the workload with --network container:<sidecar> --cap-drop ALL, and set OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_MODE=dns+nft and OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_RULES={defaultAction:deny,...}. Pin the image by digest. AISEF probes must then verify that IP-literal, DoH, host-gateway and sibling-container connections are refused.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not use dns-only mode (it gates names only). Do not copy the silent fallback to dns-only on an invalid mode (main.go:223-230); AISEF should fail closed. Do not allow any workload capability that permits SO_MARK (NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW), because marked packets bypass both redirect and nft. Do not share a writable /opt/opensandbox volume between workload and sidecar. Do not rely on the schema docstring's 'empty = allow-all'; state defaultAction explicitly.

mechanisms.name: Hardened Docker host-config builder
mechanisms.how: _base_host_config_kwargs sets network_mode, security_opt (no-new-privileges, optional apparmor= and seccomp=), cap_drop (9-cap default list), pids_limit (4096), mem_limit and nano_cpus, GPU device requests and an optional OCI runtime (runsc/kata). A startup resolver checks that the runtime exists.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use it as a checklist for AISEF's own docker-run profile, and go stricter: --cap-drop ALL, a non-root --user, --read-only plus tmpfs /tmp, an explicit seccomp profile, --pids-limit/--memory/--cpus, no published ports, and runsc where the network design allows it.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: OSB omits user, read-only rootfs and tmpfs, keeps Docker-default caps not on its list, and defaults network_mode to 'host' when unset. Do not inherit those defaults.

mechanisms.name: Fail-closed host-path allowlist with realpath re-check
mechanisms.how: Host bind mounts must lie under configured absolute prefixes; an empty list rejects all. '..' and non-normalized paths are rejected, then realpath of both the path and the prefixes is re-checked against symlink escape.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use the pattern for mounting only the candidate worktree into the developer sandbox and only the frozen candidate plus hidden bundle into the verifier sandbox.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Validation-time realpath leaves a TOCTOU window. Prefer controller-created directories the workload cannot write before mount, or copy-in (put_archive) instead of binds for hidden material. Do not keep the unrestricted named-volume ('pvc') backend.

mechanisms.name: In-sandbox execution daemon (execd) injected at create time
mechanisms.how: The server copies execd, bootstrap.sh, bwrap and the launcher from the execd image into the container via put_archive and overrides the entrypoint. execd serves HTTP on :44772 for /command, /files, /pty, /code and /session, plus a /proxy/{port} reverse proxy. Auth is an optional X-EXECD-ACCESS-TOKEN, or a token hash delivered by an unauthenticated /internal/init.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Mostly a negative lesson. AISEF's controller should drive execution with `docker exec` or the Docker API (over SSH or a unix socket the workload cannot reach) rather than a network daemon inside the untrusted container. If OSB is adopted anyway, execd ports must be reachable only from the controller (publish_host=127.0.0.1 plus SSH tunnel) and untrusted sandboxes must have dns+nft deny so they cannot reach peers' execd.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Do not copy an unauthenticated /internal/init that can rebind credentials. Do not copy the default no-token mode. Do not pass tokens through the container env. Do not use a local root daemon that accepts commands without a uid from any local process.

mechanisms.name: Explicit-acknowledgement startup guard
mechanisms.how: Starting without server.api_key requires typing YES on a TTY or setting OPENSANDBOX_INSECURE_SERVER=YES; otherwise startup aborts.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Use the pattern for AISEF executor config: refuse to start an isolation backend when a safety-critical setting (network mode, egress mode, publish host, user) is in its insecure default, unless an explicit, journaled override is present.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Note that it guards only the API key. It does not guard network_mode=host, egress mode=dns or publish_host=0.0.0.0.

mechanisms.name: Workload env scrubbing of daemon credentials
mechanisms.how: A blacklist (EXECD_ACCESS_TOKEN, JUPYTER_TOKEN, EXECD_ENVS, ...) is removed from the environment of every user process that execd spawns.
mechanisms.aisef_use: Apply the same idea when the controller launches the coding client: build an explicit allowlist env, not inherit-and-strip.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Env stripping is not a boundary when the workload shares a uid with the credential holder (/proc/<pid>/environ). Use an allowlist and separate uids or containers.

mechanisms.name: Per-sandbox TTL with restore-on-restart
mechanisms.how: Each sandbox gets an expires_at label and an in-process Timer. On server restart, expirations are rebuilt from container labels and expired sandboxes are removed.
mechanisms.aisef_use: A hard wall-clock cap per developer or verifier sandbox, as a backstop to AISEF's own budget/time limits.
mechanisms.do_not_copy: Keep kill/delete authority in AISEF's independent controller view (per AISEF INV-MUTATION-AUTHORITY), not in a backend that workload-reachable APIs could influence. Record OSB expiry as an observed event, not as an AISEF decision.

research.adapter_contract:
Design rules for an AISEF `execution` backend, whether OpenSandbox or a plain hardened `docker run`.

1. Threat model. Developer/candidate code is untrusted. The OSB server is root-equivalent (Docker socket) and belongs to the trusted controller side. It runs only on the Linux executor host and listens on 127.0.0.1 behind an SSH tunnel from macOS.

2. If OSB is used, set at minimum:
   - server.api_key set, and server.host=127.0.0.1.
   - docker.network_mode='bridge' set explicitly; the code default is 'host'.
   - docker.publish_host='127.0.0.1'.
   - egress.mode='dns+nft'. Validate it at AISEF startup and refuse 'dns'.
   - Every untrusted sandbox created with networkPolicy {defaultAction:'deny', egress:[allow only the provider domains and mirrors]}.
   - docker.drop_capabilities includes NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW (SO_MARK bypass).
   - no_new_privileges=true; pids_limit set; resourceLimits memory/cpu always set.
   - Never enable extensions bootstrap.execd.isolation.
   - allowed_host_paths limited to a controller-owned worktree root.
   - Pin execd and egress images by digest.

3. Because execd is unauthenticated (N4) and /internal/init can rebind its token (N5), AISEF must not treat execd auth as a boundary. Reachability control is the boundary: deny policy on every untrusted sandbox, and localhost-only publishing.

4. Never use the server proxy route as a security boundary. It skips API-key auth in single-tenant mode.

5. The verifier/hidden bundle lives in a separate sandbox created after the candidate is frozen, or in a controller-owned container outside OSB. It also gets a deny-all egress policy. Hidden material is copied in, never mounted from a named volume or shared path.

6. Run the agent with a non-root image USER. OSB never sets the container user, and a non-root uid gives no protection while a local root execd accepts commands (N7).

7. V2-05 acceptance probes, run from inside the developer sandbox; each must be denied:
   - TCP to 172.17.0.0/16:44772 and to host-gateway:8080 and 40000-60000.
   - IP-literal HTTPS to a non-allowlisted address.
   - DoH to 1.1.1.1:443.
   - Reading /proc/1/environ for controller secrets.
   - Listing the Docker socket.
   - Reading any verifier or hidden path.
   Also confirm that the allowlisted provider is reachable. Record OSB version, image digests and config hash with each run.

8. Default recommendation: an AISEF-owned hardened `docker run`, optionally with OSB's egress image reused standalone as a netns sidecar. Use it over the full OSB server+execd stack until the probes in rule 7 pass on OSB. A plain run has fewer network-exposed components: no execd daemon, no unauthenticated proxy, and the controller uses docker exec.

Plain profile: --user 10001:10001 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --security-opt seccomp=<profile> --pids-limit N --memory/--cpus --network container:<egress-sidecar> or none, -v <worktree>:/work:rw only, no -p, driven via DOCKER_HOST=ssh://executor.
risks: execd runs with no authentication on the Docker backend by default (N4). Its /internal/init endpoint can replace any configured token without credentials (N5). With publish_host defaulting to 0.0.0.0 (N6), anyone who can reach the executor's ports 40000-60000 can run commands in any sandbox, including a verifier holding hidden tests.

Sandboxes on the shared default Docker bridge can reach each other's execd by container IP. Only dns+nft egress deny prevents this, and egress defaults to dns-only (N8), which does not block IP-literal connections.
A config with no [docker] section falls back to network_mode='host' (N1). In host mode networkPolicy is rejected and sandboxes can reach every service on the host's loopback.

The server proxy route /sandboxes/{id}/proxy/{port} is reachable without an API key in single-tenant mode (N3), and Docker has no secure-access option. The only protection is keeping the UUID sandbox ID secret.
The egress sidecar silently falls back to dns-only on an invalid mode string (fail-open). Packets carrying the egress mark bypass enforcement, so NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW must stay dropped (N9).

OSB does not set a container user, read-only rootfs or tmpfs (N12). Isolation sessions add SYS_ADMIN and unconfined seccomp/AppArmor (N13). The execd hardening floor is off by default and fails open (N14).

Docs and code disagree in several places: schema docstring 'empty egress = allow-all' vs code default deny (N10), and the example config 'empty allowed_host_paths = all allowed' vs code reject-all (N11). Trust code, and re-verify on each upgrade.
The project changes fast (3271 commits; HEAD 2026-10-01) and examples use mutable image tags; the execd Dockerfile builds bwrap from alpine:latest. Pin digests and re-audit before each bump.

The OSB server needs the Docker socket, so compromising the server or its API key means root on the executor host. CORS is allow_origins=* with credentials (N2), which matters if the server ever runs without an api_key on a workstation.
Licensing: Apache-2.0 with no NOTICE. Redistributing the execd image also redistributes a static LGPL bubblewrap binary (INFERENCE from upstream bubblewrap's license).
The proposal's OSB-1 'redirect' claim is only partly verified. Both URLs serve identical refs via git, but no HTTP 3xx was observed at the git layer (P9).
Nothing was executed. All security conclusions come from static reading at c7dc78a. N5/N7 exploitability and the egress bypasses are unverified until AISEF runs the rule-7 probes in an isolated lab.
